NASA Ozone Watch: Ozone hole facts (https://ozonewatch.gsfc.nasa.gov/facts/hole_SH.html)
Successful web open; Total lines: 48; captured 2026-10-19.
L0-L20: NASA GSFC Ozone Watch navigation and topics.
L21: What is the Ozone Hole?
L22: The ozone hole is a region of exceptionally depleted ozone in the stratosphere over the Antarctic at the beginning of Southern Hemisphere spring (August–October); satellite image centered over Antarctica.
L23: Total column ozone below 220 Dobson Units was not observed before 1979; field mission data associate below 220 DU with catalyzed ozone loss; NASA uses 220 DU as the boundary of the region representing ozone loss.
L24: The area is calculated from daily total-column ozone snapshots enclosed by the 220-DU line.
L25-L26: image and whitespace.
L27: The ozone hole is the region over Antarctica with total ozone of 220 Dobson Units or lower; map data from NASA Aura/OMI.
L28-L31: CFC and chlorine overview.
L32: Polar stratospheric clouds and ozone.
L33: Winter polar vortex isolates Antarctic air; darkness and cold permit clouds to form.
L34: Chemical reactions occur on polar stratospheric cloud particles.
L35-L37: PSC particles provide a surface for reactions freeing chlorine in Antarctic stratosphere.
L38: Return of sunlight in October releases chlorine that destroys ozone catalytically.
L39: Ozone hole grows through early spring until warming weakens vortex and surrounding air mixes in.
L40-L42: NASA official, curator and last updated 2024-09-23.
L43-L47: site footer/credit.

Scientific Assessment of Ozone Depletion 2022: Twenty Questions and Answers About the Ozone Layer (https://csl.noaa.gov/assessments/ozone/2022/twentyquestions/)
Successful bounded web open at line 452; page total 1101 lines; full visible window L426-L502 returned 2026-10-19.
L452: Q11 Is there depletion of the Arctic ozone layer?
L453: Yes, significant Arctic depletion occurs in most years in late winter/early spring (Jan–Mar), is less severe than Antarctica, and varies more year to year.
L454: Even the most severe Arctic depletion does not reach Antarctic-low total ozone; an extensive recurrent ozone hole as found in Antarctic stratosphere does not occur in Arctic.
L455-L462: Arctic depletion mechanism and variability.
L463-L468: Arctic observations; Antarctic low values not routine in Arctic.
L469-L476: unusually strong Arctic depletion in 1997, 2011 and 2020; cold conditions and strong vortex favorable to strong loss.
L477-L480: Arctic layer retains substantial ozone despite depletion.
L481-L483: 2020 was exceptionally depleted; chemical loss over Arctic vortex was similar in magnitude to regular Antarctic loss, while measured Arctic ozone remained above routine Antarctic values.
L484-L491: Antarctic near-complete depletion is common; Arctic profiles and measurements.
L492-L502: beginning of Q12 on nonpolar depletion.
rawSources.coverage: Q11 L452-L491 directly supports distinction between annual Antarctic hole and substantial but variable Arctic ozone depletion.

literal.prompt: Над какой полярной областью каждую весну наблюдают озоновую дыру?

literalGroups.primaryGround: NASA L22,L27 locates seasonal ozone hole over Antarctica; NOAA Q11 L452-L457 distinguishes it from Arctic depletion. All options are genuine polar places; only Antarctica answers the question.

literalGroups.literal: Это Антарктика. Весной Южного полушария очень холодный полярный вихрь создаёт условия для быстрого разрушения стратосферного озона.
literalGroups.primaryGround: NASA L22 places the event in Southern Hemisphere spring; L33-L39 connects winter cold, polar vortex/PSC chemistry, sunlight return and ozone destruction.

literalGroups.literal: Над Арктикой тоже бывает сильное истощение озона, но ежегодную озоновую дыру связывают прежде всего с Антарктикой.
literalGroups.primaryGround: NOAA Q11 L453-L456 says Arctic depletion occurs in most years but is less severe/more variable; L469-L474 records rare strong episodes. The note’s distinction is accurate.

literalGroups.literal: NASA определяет границу озоновой дыры по общему содержанию озона не выше 220 единиц Добсона.
literalGroups.primaryGround: NASA L27 explicitly defines the Antarctic ozone-hole region by total ozone <=220 DU. This adds a measurable own-option fact beyond the prompt/key.

literalGroups.literal: Гренландия лежит в Арктике, но не является центром ежегодной антарктической озоновой дыры.
literalGroups.primaryGround: NOAA PMEL L247 includes Greenland in the Arctic; NASA L22,L27 places ozone-hole region over Antarctica.

literalGroups.literal: Аляска находится в высоких северных широтах, далеко от области антарктической озоновой дыры.
literalGroups.primaryGround: NOAA PMEL L247 includes northern Alaska in the Arctic; NASA L22,L27 locates the ozone-hole region over Antarctica.
